about: The tractus of the formulary “Saint Anne, Mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s02.translation: Come, O spouse of Christ, receive the crown which the Lord has prepared for you forever. You have loved justice and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions. In your splendor and your beauty, set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

w045.explanation: The repeated name identifies the same subject: God, the addressee’s God, performs the anointing.

w050.explanation: Above expresses a comparison with the companions, not a spatial position or the agent of the anointing.

w058.explanation: The closing sequence gives three commands. Here the first urges the addressee to set forward. No bow, horse, or chariot is named in the Latin.
